newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO CORN FUTURES SURGE ON CBOT RALLY.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO CORN FUTURES SURGE ON CBOT RALLY.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply higher on Wednesday due to heavy buying triggered by an overnight rally in Chicago, traders said.
All contracts surged by their 600 yen per tonne daily limit at the opening and remained glued to their limits throughout the day.
Benchmark July 1998 closed up 600 yen at 14,630 yen per tonne while limitless spot September 1997 ended up 950 yen at 15,920 yen at the close.
On Tuesday, the USDA estimated U.S. 1997 corn production would be around 9.276 billion bushels, sharply below its forecast of 9.7 billion in July.
The September corn futures on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) ended the 12-cent limit up, at $2.61-3/4 per bushel.
"Everybody rushed to buy corn today, that's all," a brokerage house trader said. "I think bullish sentiment will remain tomorrow."
The spot September expires on Friday. Open interest in the contract was 5,509 lots as of August 12.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system rose to $2.72-1/2 per bushel at 0630 GMT, against $2.61-3/4 at Tuesday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.45-1/2 per bushel at 0630 GMT, against $7.43-3/4 at Tuesday's close.
